prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of the 2017 Manifesto (policies only)

Brexit and sovereignty
- Six tests for exit: restore full UK lawmaking and end ECJ/ECHR jurisdiction; full control of migration and borders; leave single market and customs union and regain independent WTO seat; restore a 200‑mile Exclusive Economic Zone and control fisheries; pay no “divorce” bill and recover UK shares of EU assets; complete by end‑2019.
- Repeal the 1972 European Communities Act; leave the Common Fisheries Policy; repeal the 1964 London Fisheries Convention; require all fish caught in UK waters to be landed in the UK; create a Fisheries Protection Force; reinstate blue passports.

Public finances and tax
- Fund priorities from: reducing foreign aid to 0.2% of GNI, scrapping HS2, replacing the Barnett Formula with needs-based funding, and ending EU contributions (total c. £35bn by 2021–22).
- Raise personal allowance to at least £13,500 and 40% threshold to £55,000; increase inheritance tax threshold to £500,000 per person (goal: abolition over time).
- Remove VAT from domestic energy and hot takeaway food; abolish the TV licence (phase-out over three years).
- Crack down on multinational tax avoidance.

Business and jobs
- Cut business rates by 20% for premises with rateable value <£50k; penalise persistent late payers; open public procurement to SMEs; no quarterly tax returns for the self‑employed.
- Require jobs to be advertised domestically first; allow preference for under‑25 local applicants; protect employment rights; tighten zero‑hours use.

Housing
- Create a Housing Development Corporation to deliver up to 100,000 factory‑built modular homes per year on brownfield sites for first‑time buyers under 40; resale back to HDC at cost-plus‑inflation; expand council housebuilding; review housing associations; release dormant public land.

NHS and social care
- Additional £11bn a year by 2021/22 (c. £9bn NHS, £2bn social care); integrate health and social care under a single department.
- Lift medical school cap to 10,000; fund tuition for medical students (service commitment); expand GP, nurse, midwife training; restore nursing bursaries; scrap hospital parking charges.
- Toughen cost recovery from ineligible users; license NHS managers; end PFI use; guarantee right to remain for existing EU health and care workers; Royal Commission on long‑term funding.

Mental health
- At least +£500m per year; 28‑day maximum wait; school‑based counselling nationwide; integrated support for forces and veterans.

Education and skills
- Open a grammar or technical school in every town; expand vocational/dual training; abolish Key Stage 1 SATs; restore maintenance grants.
- Abolish tuition fees for STEM (and medical with NHS commitment) tied to working in the UK; stronger careers and employability education; reverse special‑school closures; universal first‑aid training.

Families and justice
- Expand wrap‑around childcare 8am–6pm; broaden eligible providers; emergency childcare registers; £80m fund to include children with SEN.
- Presumption of shared parenting; greater family‑court transparency.

Older and disabled people
- Maintain pensioner benefits and the triple lock; invest up to £2bn/year in social care; protect community services; improve care workforce pay/conditions; national dementia plan (+£400m/yr); reform disability assessments; raise Carer’s Allowance; scrap the bedroom tax.

Migration and integration
- Target net migration to balance over five years via a non‑discriminatory points‑based and permit system; five‑year pause on low‑skilled migration; seasonal worker visas; four visa classes (work, visitor, student, family).
- Five years of tax/NI before access to most benefits and non‑urgent NHS; no amnesty; +4,000 border staff; rights to remain for EU residents present before Article 50.
- One law for all; commission to disband sharia councils; ban full‑face coverings in public places; tougher action on FGM, forced marriage, “honour” crimes; stronger school oversight against extremism.

Policing and prisons
- +20,000 police and +7,000 prison officers; restore Stop and Search; keep existing prisons open; deport foreign offenders; tighter control of drugs and extremism in prisons.

Foreign policy, defence, veterans
- Meet a genuine 2% of GDP on defence plus +£1bn/year by 2021/22; +20,000 personnel; retain nuclear deterrent; oppose EU military integration.
- Create a Veterans’ Administration; hostels and housing allocations; guaranteed jobs in police/prison/border services for eligible leavers; curb historical legal pursuit of veterans.
- Support territories’ self‑determination; deepen Commonwealth and US ties; cautious on interventions; pursue Israel‑Palestine peace; conditionally improve relations with Russia.

Trade and aid
- Reduce aid to 0.2% of GNI; close DFID; focus on disaster relief, health, water, and accountable projects; prioritise free trade deals including with developing nations; commission a 500‑bed hospital ship.

Transport
- Scrap HS2; oppose Heathrow third runway; upgrade existing rail including east‑west links in the North; remove/oppose road tolls; expand EV charging; protect diesel owners from new penalties; support rural buses; freeze then aim to cut/abolish Air Passenger Duty; introduce a “Britdisc” for foreign vehicles.

Environment, food, energy
- New Environmental Protection Act; stronger protection for ancient woodlands; promote urban green space and permeable surfaces; tackle plastic waste (consider deposit return).
- Replace CAP with a capped Single Farm Payment favouring active, smaller, hill and organic farms; incentivise reduced antibiotics; ban live exports; CCTV in abattoirs; clear slaughter‑method labelling; tougher cruelty penalties.
- Repeal the Climate Change Act; leave Paris Agreement and EU ETS; diversify energy mix including shale (not in national parks); remove green levies as contracts expire; cut prepayment and paper‑billing penalties.
